MAJOR: Empty-delta rule excludes `engineering/**` and "derived docs" categorically; any review-relevant content placed under those paths (e.g., hand-edited decisions under engineering/) silently skips re-review with no model call. Exclusions must be content-class-based (generated/design-render only), not path-prefix-based.

DELTA_NO_CODE_CHANGE outcome is underspecified: design says "no model call, previous reviewed head stays as delta base," but does not state whether evidence is written, whether head tracking advances, or what the gate exit/report shows. Ambiguity here risks evidence-boundary drift and un-auditable "accepted without review" states.

Test matrix AC-4 relies on "existing gate tests" for review/gate render, but the recurring ledger explicitly flags that `_render_review`/`_item_dispositions` have no coverage (index alignment, missing-item, unknown-status). The design repeats a known gap instead of adding the missing tests.

Encoding gate applies UTF-8 validation to all changed files including worktree/untracked with no binary/asset exemption; image/font/archive assets will false-positive. "Generated files BOM-free" mitigation does not cover third-party or binary files.

Concurrency/multi-instance safety of `last_reviewed_head` update is not addressed: two concurrent re-reviews on the same item can race the advance; "collisions resolve by latest at" uses wall-clock (recurring nit), which is not a safe ordering guarantee under clock skew.
MINOR: First-review merge-base..HEAD assumes a resolvable merge base; shallow clones / orphan branches will fail without a defined fallback (fail closed vs. full-HEAD review).

Evidence redaction stores a "reason hash" but the contract does not specify retention/expiry of the `<item>-<diff_sha>.json` evidence set; unbounded accumulation of review artifacts will bloat the repo over time.
Hard-coded file exclusions (`config/id-blocks.json`, "architect-review baseline") in the empty-delta rule are brittle; move to a declarative exclusion list in `config/` for adaptability.
AC-4 test kind "logic" is undefined in the test matrix vocabulary (unit/integration/e2e); ambiguous whether it executes in CI or is a manual review checklist.
Design-pack `enforce_from` migration is stated as "explicit" but no rollout test asserts that pre-enforcement items pass Gate 1 unchanged (regression risk when the date boundary is crossed).
NIT: Wall-clock nanosecond probe-key uniqueness persists as a recurring nit; a monotonically-incremented counter or sha-based key removes it permanently.

Observability relies solely on stderr/exit codes and trail JSON; for a long-lived review toolchain, a lightweight structured log line (item, mode, base, head, outcome) would ease retroactive analysis without new infrastructure.
`DELTA_NO_CODE_CHANGE` sits in the failure matrix though it is an accept path; consider renaming to an outcome/status namespace to avoid confusion in gate dashboards.
SUMMARY: Solid, well-scoped design: delta review semantics, design-pack enforcement, and encoding gate are the right things, with sound guardrail coverage (fail-closed, disposition ownership, revert-based rollback).
Top risks: over-broad empty-delta exclusions that can silently skip reviews, undefined evidence/state handling for data-only commits, and a test plan that restates known coverage gaps as covered.
Recommend tightening delta-exclusion classification, specifying the no-change evidence contract, and adding the missing render/disposition tests before Gate 1.5.
